brief: A tool rack that hangs on a wall from keyhole hangers, with hooks for small hand tools.

requirements.requirement: Tool rack that hangs on a wall from keyhole hangers
requirements.evidence: Two piece cells at (0,0,0) and (-1,0,0), each with a hex-acc-keyhole accessory (accessory:0#0,0#0 and accessory:0#-1,0#3) on the same face-slot pattern, so both hangers sit on the wall side. A joint bolt (jointBolt:0#-1,0#0) locks the two cells together so they hang as one unit. Not verified: the keyhole orientation was not visually confirmed, since look reports no geometry.
Four hook accessories: hex-acc-hook on slots 1 and 2 of each cell (accessory:0#0,0#1, 0#0,0#2, 0#-1,0#1, 0#-1,0#2). Each hook plate carries two hooks, giving eight hook positions in total.

requirements.requirement: Wall-hung, the rack itself is a finished, closed build
requirements.evidence: capOpenFaces added solid caps to the open faces of both cells; check_build reports meshClash clear and no issues.

finish.summary: A two-cell tool rack: two cells joined by a joint bolt, each with a keyhole hanger on its back and two hook plates on its front for small hand tools. check_build is clear (no issues, meshClash clear). I did not check the hook spacing against specific tools, and the material and load capacity of the printed hooks are not verified.

lines.label: M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

events.text: The base piece offers six accessory slots. I'll try a keyhole hanger on slot 0 and two hook plates on slots 1 and 2, then check the result.
All three accessories were placed. I'll run the configurator checks and look at the piece from the front.

result.note: ok covers rule errors only. meshClash must read "clear" for the meshes to be checked and clear.

events.text: The check is clear, with only an info note about three open faces. Next I'll apply the house rules, cap the open faces and lock the joints, then check again.

result.note: ok covers rule errors only. meshClash must read "clear" for the meshes to be checked and clear.

events.text: The cap step was rolled back as a whole batch, because lockJoints had nothing to join on a single cell. I'll look at the piece placement sockets, since a second cell with its own keyhole would make the rack hang more evenly.
I'll add a second cell next to the first, then find the keyhole and hook sockets on it.

warnings.message: 1 part(s) could slide apart (1 piece(s)); joint bolts lock them.

events.text: The new cell offers keyhole sockets on several faces. I'll place a keyhole on its slot 3 (the face opposite slot 0, matching the first keyhole) and check the mesh.

issues.message: 1 part(s) could slide apart (1 piece(s)); joint bolts lock them.

events.text: The two cells are not yet joined, so the configurator flags them as a loose body. I'll look for a joint bolt socket between them.

result.note: ok covers rule errors only. meshClash must read "clear" for the meshes to be checked and clear.

events.text: The joint is in and the check is clear. Next I'll add hook plates to the new cell.
I'll add hook plates on slots 1 and 2 of the new cell, matching the first cell, then cap the open faces and check.

result.note: ok covers rule errors only. meshClash must read "clear" for the meshes to be checked and clear.

events.text: The check is clean. I'll look at the rack from the front and from behind to confirm the keyholes and hooks are on the correct faces.
The rack is built and passes the configurator checks. The `look` tool reports no visible props, so I could not confirm the orientation visually. I'm finishing here.
